source_evidence: Exact player 'let’s have us a look shall we' authorizes ordinary inspection of the just-defeated hunters' visible hillside refuge, not an automatic hazardous extended expedition, expenditure or claim on goods. At~11:01–11:10 Day331, V and willing Cirren/Fenar approach along the existing rough slope to the visible fissure; Mara voluntarily remains with stopped coach and four healthy horses. Newly fixed immediate physical geography: natural limestone fissure about5ft wide at mouth, opening into one low irregular shelter about25ft deep and15ft wide at widest, roots and small upper daylight gap allow ordinary visual inspection of back wall without a torch or spell; no concealed passage, additional creature, separate encounter, active trap or impassable obstacle. The finite previously fixed three aberrant hunters had used this local refuge. Ordinary visible findings: three separate flattened bedding hollows with dry grass/deerskin, heaps of animal bones and gnawed deer/livestock-sized remains, crude antler hooks, whetstone and scavenged worn harness buckles/straps. No identified humanoid remains or living captive, no obvious valuables or magical object, no verified source of harness, ownership, kill date, additional faction, specific ancient origin or ancestry link. No further lair beyond visible end; Cirren observes these creatures appear to have made a living here rather than merely wandered from a portal, but species and broader history remain uncertain. Fenar observes visible end of shelter, no additional threat present. No contested search, hidden clue, identification, coin roll, attack, new healing or spell; all are plainly visible during the ordinary look. No goods collected, corpses searched or stripped, ownership assumed, food/feed charged, coach moved, or full day travel concluded. Party at accessible fissure with Mara nearby above, next V decision whether inspect/take further action or return to road. Actual campaign time about11:10, unchanged HP/resources; LR0/6.
